title.narrative: Health Services Sector Development Program, Subprogram 1

description.narrative: The Health Services Sector Development Program (HSSDP) will help Papua New Guinea (PNG) strengthen health services through policy reforms and direct investments in health systems. A diagnostic assessment of the coverage, financing, and quality of health services is required to ensure that the interventions are designed for maximum impact.

description.narrative: A more sustainable and efficient health care system achieved

By 2028, proportion (%) of births attended by skilled personnel at health facilities for all target facility catchments on average is 10% greater than the national average for calendar year 2026 (2021 baseline: 26% less than the national average) Progress/Status: 36.4% in 2023 - 39.0% for 6 months Jan to June 2024. This is a positive trend but insufficient to ensure attainment of the target by 2027-2028. Challenge is also on getting the accurate catchment population. Data Source: Annual DOH SPAR reports; National Health Information System SPAR Reports Actual value:

By 2028, proportion (%) of children under 1 year of age who have received three doses of DPT3-Hib-HepB vaccine for all target facility catchments on average is 10% greater than the national average for calendar year 2026 Progress/Status: 40.6% in 2023 - 43.6% for 6 months Jan to June 2024. Positive trend but insufficient to ensure achievement of this outcome by 2027-2028. Data Source: Annual DOH SPAR reports; National Health Information System SPAR Reports Actual value:

By 2028, at least 80% of average annual provincial health expenditure as a proportion of estimated need for 2027-2028 Progress/Status: Progress with the achievement of this outcome has been constrained by PNG's current fiscal position. While the available funds for the Health Sector have been increasing in recent years, the increase is mostly attributable to capital funding of major Provincial Hospitals. Data Source: Annual DOH SPAR reports Actual value:

By 2028, whole-genome sequencing, disaggregated by sex and including bioinformatics, established for the surveillance of national and regional emerging infections and public health threats Progress/Status: This is an initiative of the National Reference Laboratory project which is yet to start. Data Source: Annual DOH SPAR reports; National Reference Laboratory Strategic Plan M&E Report Base year: 2022
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Health service delivery components strengthened Indicator: Programmatic approach The percentage of project facilities requisitioning monthly from the area medical stores increased to at least 85% for 2022‒2026 Achievement: 85 Progress/Status: The individual Consultant and the Consulting Firm working on strategies to improve the reliability of the Medical Supplies Procurement and Distribution Service completed the drafting of a Master Plan for this purpose and the Plan was considered and endorsed by the National Department of Health's Senior Executive Management (SEM) Group. The Master Plan is referenced in the National Health Plan 2021-2030 and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for the procurement and management of medical supplies stock have been developed, endorsed and circulated to the Provincial Health Authorities and within the Department. Further high-level meeting to be convened by Minister on 27 January 2026 to advance planning for major reform. Data Source: DOH electronic health information system

Output: Subnational health system management strengthened Indicator: At least 10 staff annually (5 males; 5 females) per province trained in budget preparation and monitoring for years 2021-2023 Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: PFM Consultant engaged since February 2020. PFM modules for PHA Manual and training materials developed and training conducted annually. This target was not achieved in 2023 due to COVID. Some training will continue but it is unlikely that they will be able to catch up. This target will likely be revised by half to 5 staff. Data Source: Annual project reports

Output: Health service delivery components strengthened Indicator: One national reference laboratory built in compliance with CEPA requirements and including disability access, male and female toilets and shower Progress/Status: Design documentation started with conceptual floor plan for discussion / review by Pathologists / Health Specialists. However, pending the National Referral Laboratory (NRL) Policy, the scope for NRL is being debated pending changes / adjustments to floor plan and functional flows.
Also, legal ownership of land for NRL is being established by NDoH for ascertaining decision for NRL location; and pending land certainty is also adding complexity to finalize the conceptual design for floor plan. Data Source: Annual project reports Actual value:

Output: Subnational health system management strengthened Indicator: At least 45 provincial laboratory personnel (at least 50% female) trained in implementing the 2021 national health service standards Achievement: 200 Progress/Status: Not started Data Source: Annual project reports

Output: Subnational health system management strengthened Indicator: Programmatic approach PHAs established in 22 provinces by 2023 Achievement: 22 Progress/Status: All 22 PHAs established by January 2020. Data Source: PHA establishment agreements

Output: Health service delivery components strengthened Indicator: eNHIS implemented and sex-disaggregated data entered in all 96 districts Progress/Status: Data collection and reporting from the point of service has been implemented in all health facilities in Hela, East New Britain, Central, Manus, New Ireland, West Sepik, Simbu, Gulf, East Sepik, Oro, Eastern Highlands, Jiwaka, Southern Highlands and Madang Provinces. Point of service data entry and reporting is now available from all 846 Level 2, 3, 4 and 5 health facilities in 22 Provinces. All data is disaggregated apart from immunization data as this is being done through a separate pilot funded by GAVI. Data Source: Annual project reports Actual value:

Output: Health service delivery components strengthened Indicator: 100% of health partnerships and MOUs in effect as of November 2017, compiled at the national and subnational levels, by province and partner category, including which partnerships have a gender equity focus Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: All PHAs have now been supported to establish Partnership Committees through HSSDP and/or RPHSDP. Data Source: DOH SPAR reports, project reports

Output: Health service delivery components strengthened Indicator: At least three level 4, eight level 3, and seven level 2 gender-sensitive health facility infrastructure upgrades completed and commissioned Progress/Status: Construction completed: Bitokara CHP in West New Britain completed in Feb 2023; Gaulim CHP completed in Nov 2022; Umba CHP completed in Oct 2022; Ambunti Health Centre completed and handed over in Oct 2022; Wirui Urban Clinic completed in June 2024. Cape Gloucester Health Centre completed and commissioned August 2025. Stages 1, 2, 3 & 4 of civil works for the Bogia District Hospital completed.
Construction works ongoing in Pomio, Kopiago, Agevairu, Warasikau, Soroken, Talyokos, Maramuni, and Bogia for stage 5.
Construction of stages 1 & 2 commenced at Buin District Hospital and for Koroba District Hospital. Bids invited for Karap Health Centre in Nov, 25.
Data Source: Annual project reports Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2017 Baseline value: N Target year: 2027 Target value: Y
